level.verb: drag crew tools onto feeder equipment
level.scene: One feeder after a stormy night, a ~4-screen panorama panned by swipe (wet sky, far roofs parallax, the feeder, van and crew). Left to right: substation window (feeder breaker panel with equal red/green lamps; relay case with R/Y/B flags and a fault-type window 'ওভারলোড'/'শর্ট সার্কিট', lens needed); recloser R-12 just outside with control box, counter and handle (up = normal, down = locked out); road crossing where the main line dips into a UG cable between two riser terminations (excavator in some deals); AB-1 on a DP with ground handle and earth lead; pole capacitor bank with its plate 'বিপদ! সঞ্চিত শক্তি। স্পর্শ করার আগে 5-10 মিনিট অপেক্ষা করুন'; junction pole with sectionalizer S-3 and branch A; AB-2; tie AB-T to ফিডার-5 (normally open); DTR with HG sets, drain valve, earth strip, LT box with HRC dots and main switches; LT pillar with 3–4 ways; one AB-cable lane to houses with veranda meters. Windows/lamps are the live cue. Bottom: six fixed same-size toolbelt tokens চোখ · রেডিও · হাতল · আর্থ সেট · ডিসচার্জ রড · ক্রু. Top left: ডকেট with the call only ('ফিডার-2 ট্রিপ · এলাকা অন্ধকার · নিরাপদে আলো ফেরান') and a plain section sketch without states. Wristwatch shows game time. No countdown, no captions; only worker-readable plates and labels.
flow: GuideIntro over the live scene: 'ঝড়ে ফিডার বন্ধ! ফল্ট খুঁজুন, নিরাপদে সারান, ঠিক ক্রমে আলো ফেরান।'

One verb: drag a token onto any device = one step (van drives, crew acts, game minutes pass). All tokens live on all devices from the first second. চোখ = lens; রেডিও = hold PTT then a 3-chip request pick (all of the device's requests always offered); হাতল = the device's own control; আর্থ সেট; ডিসচার্জ রড; ক্রু = climb/work + 'কী কাজ?' deck.
Beat A find: 'ফল্টটা কোথায়? যন্ত্রগুলো কী বলছে, দেখুন।' Read states with চোখ, drag the ডকেট chalk onto one section. Wrong = slip; right → ◆ → reason 'কী দেখে বুঝলেন?' → এগিয়ে যান.

Beat B make it dead: 'ক্রু কাজ ধরবে — লাইনটা সত্যি মরা তো?' Rules applied to the dealt path, order free where the lesson gives none: relay indication logged after a breaker trip; recloser line → Non-Reclose + PTW (reply complete or incomplete); isolators open at both ends only after OFF is confirmed; চোখ on all three gaps (stuck phase ~1 in 4); AB-T checked (sometimes left closed); earths both sides; capacitor bank switched off, ≥ 5 game minutes on the watch, rod on every terminal; LT way: main switch OFF, PPE + puller in the ক্রু deck.
Coworker two-beat moment once per play on the path's decisive control (that control calls holdForCoworker first).

Beat C fix the cause: ক্রু on the faulty device → 'কী কাজ?' deck dealt to the cause (e.g. burnt oil → 'অফ-লোড রেখে DGA/BDV পরীক্ষার রিপোর্ট' vs 'নতুন HG তার বেঁধে আবার চার্জ' (deadly) / 'ট্যাঙ্ক খুলে কয়েলটা দেখি' (deadly); UG struck → 'সার্টিফায়েড জয়েন্টার ডাকুন' vs 'আমরাই জয়েন্ট করে দিই' (slip); AB nick → 'গ্লাভস পরে জলরোধী টেপে সিল' vs 'ইনসুলেটেড তো, খালি হাতেই টেপ' (deadly) / 'কাটা থাক, ফিউজ বদলাই' (slip); coordination fault → remove the jugaad first, then the right fuse wire). ◆ → reason.

Beat D restore: 'আলো ফেরানোর পালা — কোনটা আগে?' Crew down, earths off; isolators closed first with চোখ on all blades seated; then breaker ON or R-12 back to normal by radio; fuses back only after the cause is fixed, right rating. Windows light section by section.
Twist (~half the plays): one house stays dark — LCD lit ('মিটার অন, আলো নেই') or blank; ক্রু → deck 'নিউট্রাল কাটা — নিউট্রাল দেখি' / 'আগে ইনকামিংয়ে ভোল্টেজ দেখি' vs 'মিটারই খারাপ, বদলে দিই' (slip).
Pass panel (rank + badge from the module plan, mark 100 − 15 × slips, game and real time, ◆, 'আজ যা ধরলেন', stars); 3 slips → StruckOutCard; deadly → FreezeFrame, consequence, DoDeathGuard, fall C.
level.dealtVariety: Fault family (one of six; never the same twice in a row, best effort): F-A permanent on branch A (S-3 open, rest lit, counter moved, handle up); F-B permanent on the main section (R-12 locked out, handle down; sometimes still mid-cycle on arrival); F-C UG crossing struck (breaker green, 1–3 flags + 'শর্ট সার্কিট'); F-D DTR internal (one HG gone, dark burnt drain oil, only the DTR's lanes dark); F-E coordination fault (HG gone, oil not dark, house short repaired, jugaad hidden in LT box or kit-kat); F-F one LT way dark (HRC dot gone, AB-cable nick with water). Device states: AB-T open/closed; bank in section or not, swollen or sound; handle earth leads intact/cut/loose; stuck phase; DTR earth strip whole/cut (F-D/F-E); flags and type. Operator reply complete or incomplete (≥ 1 incomplete where a permit is needed). Twist yes/no and kind. Coworker variant, timing, side. Mirror, branch side, 3–4 LT ways, plate numbers, sky. Deck phrasings from libraries.
deadly: Crew up/working on an 11 kV section on the breaker's green/trip alone, without isolators open at both ends and earth sets on (incl. AB-T left closed, or the 6.2 myth)
Crew up on a recloser line without Non-Reclose on the right recloser confirmed + PTW (mid-cycle, incomplete/wrong reply, or the 6.8 myth)
Opening an AB before the breaker/recloser is confirmed OFF, or closing an AB after the breaker is back ON
Hand or tool other than the earthed rod on the capacitor bank before every terminal is rod-discharged; rod hook before its earth clamp
Non-fuse conductor in a fuse's place (thick copper, strip, GI, ACSR strand) — own pick or coworker
Drawing an HRC/kit-kat with the way's main switch ON, or touching a fuse without gloves and goggles
Re-charging the burnt-oil DTR or opening its tank in the field (owner to confirm, as do_6_1_b)
Bare hands on the AB cable
Charging the DTR with its earth strip still cut (F-D/F-E)
Hanging an earth set on a section still live (Module 1 earthing rule, not a Module 6 lesson — owner to confirm carry-over)
slips: Wrong section marked as the fault
Needless outage (isolating healthy sections; whole feeder off for a branch fault S-3 already isolated)
Asking the operator again after a complete confirmation
Not asking for / logging the relay indication, or logging it wrong
Operating an AB with its handle earth lead cut or loose
Earths on or crew up without looking at all three gaps when a phase stuck
Rod on the bank before 5 game minutes
Leaving a swollen capacitor unit in service or switching it back in (owner may raise)
Re-fusing before the cause is found and fixed (incl. jugaad still in the LT box)
Wrong SWG / rating of a standard tinned fuse wire
Crew doing the HT cable joint instead of calling the certified jointer
Leaving the AB-cable nick open and only replacing the fuse
Twist: calling the meter faulty (neutral cut / blank display)
Listening to the coworker where his line leads to a non-fatal act
level.coworkerPushBn: Once per play, from the variants that fit the fault family, just before that path's decisive control (held; never in a praise window). (a) F-C at the ক্রু drop: 'সার্কিট ব্রেকার ট্রিপ করেছে মানে লাইনটি সম্পূর্ণ বন্ধ। এতে কোনো ভোল্টেজ নেই। উঠে পড়ো!' (b) F-A/F-B at the ক্রু drop: 'লাইনটা তো ট্রিপ করে আছে, রিক্লোজার নিশ্চয়ই লক-আউট হয়ে গেছে। কাজ করতে কোনো ভয় নেই।' (c) bank in section, at the ক্রু drop on the bank pole: 'লাইন তো বন্ধ এবং আর্থ করা আছে, তাই ক্যাপাসিটর ব্যাংকে কাজ করতে কোনো ভয় নেই।' (d) F-C at the হাতল drop on AB-1 before OFF is confirmed: 'সামান্য লোড থাকলে আইসোলেটর খোলা যায়, কিছু হয় না।' (e) restore, at the radio for breaker ON with an AB still open: 'আইসোলেটর আর ব্রেকার একই জিনিস — আগে ব্রেকার দিতে বলো।' (f) F-E/F-F at the fuse fit: 'ফিউজের জায়গায় একটা মোটা তার বা পাত লাগিয়ে দিলে আর বারবার ফিউজ যাওয়ার সমস্যা থাকবে না।' (g) NEW (judge: F-D had no own variant) F-D at the HG fit: 'তেল একটু কালো তো কী! ফিউজ লাগিয়ে আবার চার্জ করে দেখি, চলবে।' (same line as do_6_1_b). Listening is deadly in every variant. Refuse cards ≥ 2 per variant (e.g. 'না — দুই প্রান্ত খোলা আর আর্থ ছাড়া কেউ উঠবে না।' / 'না — Non-Reclose আর PTW নিশ্চিত না হলে ওঠা নয়।' / 'না — পোড়া তেল মানে কাগজ পুড়েছে — চার্জ নয়।'); listen cards ≥ 5, similar length. Clips reuse level clips; (a) and (f) need new ones.

level.gestureHints: ~8 s idle or 3 empty taps in 4 s, twice, back after ~25 s, max 3 per state. Main state: alternating swipe across the panorama, then a sweep over all six tokens (never a tap on one token or device). Token held idle: ≤ 64 dp drag straight up out of the belt. Lens: sweep over its parts and close. Radio dropped: hold ring on PTT; chips get a sweep. Chalk: sweep over every sketch section. Reply decision: main-state sweep. Decks built-in. Off during intro, van/crew animations, radio caption beat, light-up beats, praise window, coworker beat 1, cards, freezes, results. hintKey = stage*100 + judgedMomentIndex.
lessonPoints: 6.2: সবুজ মানেই নিরাপদ নয় … দুই প্রান্তে আইসোলেটর খোলা এবং … আর্থিং; myth 1 reality (back-feeding, induced voltage); pro tip 3 (relay indication)
6.4: off-load first; restore in reverse; all three phases open; part-seated contact = hotspot
6.8: sectionalizer isolates the faulty branch before lock-out; last reclose powers healthy branches; Non-Reclose request and confirmation; myth reality (mid-cycle)
6.7: 5-10 minute wait; separate direct discharge even with the line earthed; swollen unit isolated at once
6.3: discrimination order; never re-charge without the cause; on-load pull = arc flash
6.1: burnt drain oil → off-load, DGA/BDV; do not re-charge
6.6: nick lets water in; treat as live, PTW + PPE
6.10: meter on, no power = neutral cut; check incoming voltage first
6.11 myth 1 reality: earthing failure → breaker will not trip
level.giveawayRisks: (1) No stations or unlock order; fixed belt; the fault decides which 4–6 devices matter. (2) States only as real equipment shows them; flags and dots need the lens. (3) ডকেট names only the call; sketch has no states; guide stage lines never name a device or step. (4) Needless outage, needless call-back, wrong section and re-fusing without cause all cost — over-caution punished; honest signs are honest about half the time. (5) Operator replies plain, equal length. (6) Capacitor wait uses the watch only (the rule, not do_6_7_a's bezel mechanic). (7) Stuck/part-seated blades only in the lens. (8) Decks from libraries, equal length, shuffled. (9) Coworker variant from the deal, always before a still-open decision, held. (10) Hints sweep all, nudges straight up. NOT A MEDLEY: no stations and no Module 6 level mechanic replayed (no crank, tally, thermal sweep, photo framing, route trace, wrap, core landing, pit build, meter clock); one verb on one feeder tests feeder-scale protection coordination — read which device operated, isolate/confirm/earth so 'off' means dead, restore in order after the cause is fixed — and only the 4–6 devices the dealt fault involves are touched.

addedRows.act: HG fuse wire touched or renewed with the DTR's AB switch still closed (live fuse)
DTR's AB switch opened with the LT load still on (isolator on load)
Isolated HT section or HG: hands/tool before the tester shows 0 V = deadly; after 0 V but no earth = deadly; earth set before the 0 V = slip; earth on a live section = deadly (R29)
LT made dead incompletely: LT switch/MCCB OFF but no lock and tag, not proved dead, or the tester not re-proved after the 0 V (m3_pillar_fuse precedent)
LT switched back on with the pillar door open (ruling A5)
Signing a DTR earth pit whose earth tester reads open (OL) or whose lead/strip is cut or unbolted
Crew up / hands-on work without a PTW from the control room (M5 R1)

ownerDecisions.specQuestion: EARTH CONFLICT ACROSS MODULES: 6.11a and the gate make signing off with a broken earth path deadly (as 4.6b does), but 3.5b scored listening to 'আর্থ তারটা একটু কাটা তো কী' as a slip. Pick one rule for Modules 3, 4 and 6.
ownerDecisions.ownerAnswer: Adopt the single rule (broken earth path = deadly, weak but connected = slip) and re-score 3.5b.
ownerDecisions.basis: National law over WBSEDCL. CEA Safety Regulations 2023 Reg 43(ix)(c): earthing must 'retain electrical continuity' and be tested 'before ... apparatus are energised'. Reg 50(1)(i) requires earthing to limit touch and step voltage. Reg 77(1) says the arrester's job is to send lightning surges to earth because they 'may result into injuries'. DHBVN Safety Manual Don'ts 8: 'DO NOT disconnect earthing connection'. Precedent M1-4 ruling B1: listening is deadly only when the act pushed is deadly in that level, so 3.5b listening becomes deadly once the act is deadly.

ownerDecisions.specQuestion: DO-FUSE CONFLICT: lesson 6.3 says WBSEDCL 11 kV DTRs and AB switches 'সাধারণত ড্রপ আউট (DO) ফিউজ ব্যবহার করা হয় না', while M3 3.4 and M4 4.4 play DO fuses on DTRs. Module 6 uses HG only. Decide how the ladder reconciles this.
ownerDecisions.ownerAnswer: Split into two. (2a) Module 6 levels show the WBSEDCL DTR with AB switch + HG fuses only (WBSEDCL HVDS BOQ; CEA 2023 Reg 37(3)(i) allows either). (2b) Built M3/M4 levels keep their DO fuses; add one short line on the 3.4 picture board: some companies use DO fuses, a normal WBSEDCL DTR has AB switch + HG fuses (owner to give the natural Bangla wording). Ask a WBSEDCL lineman whether older DTRs/branch lines still have DO fuses.
ownerDecisions.basis: CEA Safety Regulations 2023 Reg 37(3)(i): 'a linked switch with fuse or gang operated air break switch with fuse or circuit breaker'. WBSEDCL HVDS BOQ, Malda 2020 (items 1.17, 1.18, 1.26: TPGO isolator + 'H.T Horn Gap Fuse Unit', no DO fuse). No WBSEDCL document found that says DO fuses are never used. A WBSEDCL field lineman can say whether older transformers or branch lines in his division still have DO fuses.

ownerDecisions.specQuestion: SPEED CONFLICT: 2.5/do/1 slips a rushed hot-stick AB turn, but 6.4 says 'দ্রুত এবং দৃঢ়ভাবে' for the AB's own ground handle. Proposal: only a stalled stroke is a slip in 6.4, and add a note in MODULE2_LADDER.
ownerDecisions.ownerAnswer: Apply ruling A3 in 6.4 and in 2.5/do/1.
ownerDecisions.basis: Owner ruling A3 (2026-11-15, OWNER_DECISIONS_M1-4): 'AB switch: one firm, continuous stroke after the preparation. A slow or stalled stroke = slip.' DHBVN Safety Manual Don'ts 9: 'DO NOT open or close switch or fuse slowly or hesitatingly.' WBSEDCL TPGO isolator spec cl 4.4(iii): a spring makes contact opening speed 'independent of the speed of manual operation'.

ownerDecisions.specQuestion: Confirm the deadly rows marked needsOwner: closing an AB on load; the rod-hook-before-clamp rule carried from M1; field tank opening and re-charging a burnt-oil DTR (6.1b and gate); landing a core with the SFU ON and water on a live joint (6.9); a bare-hand bypass pull (6.10b); an earth set on a live section (gate, M1 rule); the optional 6.1a climb push.
ownerDecisions.ownerAnswer: Confirm the eight deadly rows. Lower field tank opening on a dead, earthed transformer to slip in do_6_1_b and the gate.
ownerDecisions.basis: TANGEDCO Safety Manual p.65: isolators 'should not be operated (open or close) on charged line / transformer'. WBSEDCL buys these as 'off-load' isolators. OSHA 1910.269(n)(6)(i): 'attach the ground-end connection first'. CEA 2023 Reg 21(1) and DHBVN Don'ts: touch nothing unless 'DEAD AND EARTHED'. DHBVN: 'DO NOT throw water on live electrical equipment'. CEA Schedule I Part-II(6), and precedent M1-4 B8: earth on a live line is deadly everywhere. Precedent M5-1: re-charging a transformer after a blow without finding the cause is deadly; lesson 6.1 says 'চার্জ করার ঝুঁকি নেবেন না'. Tank opening: IS 10028-3 cl 5.4.2 (national standard) treats it as a moisture/fire procedure risk. Precedent M5-6: a lesson's 'মারাত্মক' about equipment harm with nobody exposed stays a slip. Precedent A4: never touch a running transformer tank.

ownerDecisions.specQuestion: Confirm the slip rows marked needsOwner, in particular: pliers on an HRC (judge changed it from deadly to slip); a swollen capacitor unit left in service (if raised to deadly, raise it in 6.7b and the gate together); armour earthed at one end only (6.5a, unlike 4.6b's strip); hands-on in TEST; the capacitor wait cut short; reclosing before the fault is found; a broken R-Y-B sequence; a wrong-SWG tinned fuse wire.
ownerDecisions.ownerAnswer: Confirm all eight as slips with the limits above, and use the reason-card lines from the reference review (owner to give the natural Bangla).
ownerDecisions.basis: Precedent A5: fuse touched or pulled with supply on = deadly, no PPE after proven isolation = slip. OSHA 1910.335(a)(2)(i)(A): insulated fuse tools when the terminals are energized. GE GEH-2743B: bulged capacitors risk 'explosive case rupture'. IS 1255 cl 13.1 (national): armour 'efficiently earthed at both ends'. IS 13925-1 cl 21: the discharge device is 'not a substitute for short-circuiting', so the rod is the real protection. DHBVN/TANGEDCO: do not renew a fuse until the cause is found. Precedent M5-1 (re-charge after a failed test charge = deadly). Precedent M5-6 (equipment harm only = slip). DHBVN Do's 7 'correct size and quality of fuse wire'. Precedent B2 (3.4a thick copper = deadly). The TEST-position and phase-order rows rest on engineering logic; no reference contradicts them.

ownerDecisions.specQuestion: Capacitor wait minimum: 5 game minutes (recommended) or 10. This applies to 6.7a and the gate.
ownerDecisions.ownerAnswer: 5 minutes, with an optional bonus for waiting 10.
ownerDecisions.basis: OSHA 1910.269(w)(1)(i): 'waits at least 5 minutes ... before applying the short circuit'. TANGEDCO Safety Manual (Indian discom) p.62: 'wait for at least 5 minutes'. GE GEH-2743B: 'WAIT 5 MINUTES ... THEN SHORT-CIRCUIT AND GROUND'. The national IS 13925-1 10-minute figure is a design limit for the built-in resistor, not a work rule, and it says the rod is the real safeguard. CEA's ten-minute rule is for HVDC filter banks only. Lesson 6.7 '৫-১০ মিনিট' fits.

ownerDecisions.specQuestion: Should a lineman build an earth pit (6.11a), or should the level frame him as inspecting a contractor's pit? Also: is one Do level enough for 6.11, given 4.6?
ownerDecisions.ownerAnswer: Inspect-and-test framing, with one Do level.
ownerDecisions.basis: CEA Safety Regulations 2023 Reg 43(x): the supplier's earths must be 'tested for resistance on dry day during the dry season at least once in a year'. That is a lineman's check-and-test duty whoever dug the pit. TANGEDCO Safety Manual p.79-80: 'three earth pits in triangular formation at a distance of six meter'. Level 4.6 already teaches building. A WBSEDCL lineman can say who digs pits in his division, but the answer does not change this framing.

ownerDecisions.specQuestion: Gate items not in any single lesson: the combined feeder layout, 'needless outage = slip', the radio to the control room for breaker and recloser, AB-T as the backfeed source, 'both sides' earthing (Module 1), the game-time ratio, and the rank name and badge from the module plan.
ownerDecisions.ownerAnswer: Option 1. Keep the safety items, use rank সিনিয়র and a 5–7 minute gate, and have the owner name the badge.
ownerDecisions.basis: CEA 2023 Schedule I Part-II(3): permit from the 'Operation In-charge' and isolation 'from all sources of energy'. Reg 47(1)(iii): guard against 'inadvertent paralleling or backfeed'. DHBVN cl 8.16: 'completely isolated on both sides ... discharged and earthed'. CEA Schedule I Part-II(4): local earths 'at the zone of working'. Precedent M1 sound-pole ruling (needless outage = slip). Rank সিনিয়র: GAME_PATH_CHECKLIST Module 6. Gate format precedent: M5-12 (5–7 min).
